messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER: SEV2 - euc2a ingress path 5xx spike and ALB handshake backlog. Pager sent to oncall-sarah and kevin-network. Link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ingress/euc2a-ingress?orgId=1
oncall-sarah: acked. seeing 5xx increase across two ALBs behind euc2a ingress; error rate ~27% over 2m window. taking lead.
kevin-network: on it, joining. any DNS symptoms?
oncall-sarah: client-side timeouts climbing too. no DNS TTL changes visible yet. cross-region routes show healthy in euc1 but euc2 is the hotspot.
mike-runtime: logs are showing a ton of TLS handshake timeouts between ALB and envoy pods: 
```
[envoy] 2026-03-14T19:23:11Z error connection reset during TLS handshake: tls: handshake failure
[nginx] 2026-03-14T19:23:12Z 502 upstream prematurely closed connection
```
kevin-network: looks like accept queue is backing up on the ENI — seeing SYN-RECV queue growth on targets. possibly kernel backlog + keepalive mismatch.
julia-pm: customer impact: several mid-market customers reporting API errors, estimated 18% of requests failing for euc2 region (ingress). No P1 escalations yet but support is seeing tickets.
oncall-sarah: immediate mitigation plan: 1) shift small percentage of traffic to euc1 as controlled weight shift 2) change ALB target group deregistration delay to speed drain 3) roll envoy pods with updated keepalive TCP options 4) add temporary healthcheck relaxation. will coordinate.
kevin-network: starting weighted Route53 traffic policy to move 20% to euc1 now. command: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc1-weight","Weight":20,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZALB","DNSName":"alb-euc1.redwood.net"}}}]}'
```
oncall-sarah: rolling with canary weight shift + monitoring. updating grafana panel.
incidents-bot: NOTE: Route53 change submitted by kevin-network at 2026-03-14T19:28:55Z.
mike-runtime: starting envoy restart on one deployment to cycle TCP settings. using strategic 10% pod rotation: 
```
kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deploy/envoy-ingress --selector=canary=true
```
will patch configmap with `tcp_keepalive_time` tweak.
kevin-network: ALB target group shows high "connection backlog" metric; draining unhealthy targets from TG-A to TG-B in same AZ to reduce per-target backlog.
oncall-sarah: support ping: adding message to affected customers via internal ops: "We're actively mitigating elevated 5xx errors in euc2; possible degraded access; working on traffic shift." :loudspeaker:
julia-pm: please capture exact customer list that reported issues for postmortem.
mike-runtime: after first canary pod restart, handshake errors dropped ~50% for that pod. envoy metrics show TLS accepts latency improved.
kevin-network: weight shift to euc1 at 20% completed, beginning gradual increase to 50% if metrics stable for 5m.
oncall-sarah: starting to see overall error rate drop from 27% -> 12% after 15m. still above baseline.
kevin-network: increased weight to 45%. moving ALB deregistration delay to 10s for faster failover: 
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:... --deregistration-delay-seconds 10
```
incidents-bot: Pager duty: acknowledged by oncall-sarah at 2026-03-14T19:31:05Z.
statuspage-bot: Draft status update created. No public status page push until confirmed mitigation.
mike-runtime: applying temporary iptables tcp_tw_reuse tuning on nodes to reduce TIME_WAIT accumulation: 
```
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_tw_reuse
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```
kevin-network: observed a subset of targets with repeated TLS handshake failures pointing to a bad kernel patch on the image deployed to euc2 nodes. cross-checking AMI build ids.
oncall-sarah: creating mitigation RFC: rollback to prior AMI on euc2 worker pool if we see persistent failures after traffic shift.
julia-pm: what's customer visible SLA risk? if we hold at 40-50% traffic out of euc2 we reduce failures but increase latency for shifted requests. need to coordinate on SLA calls.
kevin-network: AMI check: euc2 node group image `ami-20260310-v3` has the new kernel. prior AMI `ami-20260228-v2` doesn't show handshake issues in staging. recommending rolling nodes back.
mike-runtime: preparing cordon+drain playbook for nodes in euc2, will do 10% at a time: 
```
for node in $(kubectl get nodes -l euc2 -o name | head -n3); do kubectl cordon $node; kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; sleep 60; done
```
incidents-bot: oncall handoff reminder: if this goes > 90 minutes escalate to SEV1 and notify leadership.
oncall-sarah: current timeline: 20m since detection. traffic shift stable, errors trending down to 8%. executing node recycle of suspect AMI next.
kevin-network: starting node recycle now for 3 nodes. monitoring ALB backlog and envoy accepts.
mike-runtime: after node recycle step 1, observed backlog and 5xx errors fall close to baseline. TLS handshake errors at pod-level drop to near-zero for recycled nodes.
julia-pm: drafting external comms for customers impacted with ETA for full mitigation ~45m.
oncall-sarah: mitigation looks effective. keeping incident open for verification. moving to recovery tasks: root cause analysis (kernel/AMI regression), backport automation for AMI gating, and runbook updates.
kevin-network: will open follow-up issue to block AMI publish until kernel handshake test passes in staging.
incidents-bot: ASSESSMENT: Impact window ~35m, peak failure rate ~27%, ~18% of requests affected for euc2. No data loss. Potential customer complaints: multiple support tickets; recommend SEV2 postmortem.
statuspage-bot: pushing internal status update to customers identified as impacted. public status page will follow postmortem.
oncall-sarah: handing off to kevin-network for next 2h post-incident monitoring, I'll update the incident doc and attach logs. closing live mitigation.
kevin-network: taking post-mitigation watch. will update in 30m.
incidents-bot: Incident thread closed for live mitigation at 2026-03-14T20:02:00Z, remaining action items moved to #eng-postmortems.
statuspage-bot: Public status: Identified, Mitigated. Root cause under investigation (network kernel regression)."
